universalaction.fast: Deep Shock. Power-plant worker Banner receives an electrical jolt which enables him to see the future.
East Winds. Seeking gold hidden in Banner's apartment, a gang awards him a Chinese mail-order bride; guest William Windom.
Knight Flight to Freedom. Michael attempts to rescue a FLAG agent caught in a Central American revolution.
Fright Knight. Michael poses as a stuntman in an effort to catch the deadly saboteur who is terrorizing a movie set.
Drivers. An all-star college quarterback collapses suddenly; Gage wants to discipline motorists who fail to yield to fire department vehicles.
School Days. The paramedics try to boost the confidence of a trainee who has doubts about his readiness to take on emergency duties in the field.
The Professor. Brackett cares for an ailing foreign dignitary; the paramedics rescue a helicopter pilot, deliver a baby and prevent a suicide jump.
Syndrome. Gage diagnoses tonsillitis for DeSoto, who claims to have had his tonsils removed; McCall is reunited with an old love (Robert Alda).
Honest. Gage's and DeSoto's stands on honesty are put to the test when people who withhold vital information experience different consequences.
Seance. A woman believes her dead sister is the cause of accidents in her home; a man is trapped underwater in his car with the doors jammed.
Boot. Station 51's mascot, Boot, won't eat; accidents befall a woman attempting to cook a meal; a man nearly dies from an aspirin overdose.
Rip-Off. The paramedics conduct several rescues under a shadow of guilt after being accused of stealing from a patient; guest Jo Anne Worley.
Audit. DeSoto must decide whether to amputate the leg of a trapped construction worker (James McEachin); nervous Gage faces an IRS tax audit.
The Wedworth Townsend Act. An assembly bill to create a paramedic program meets opposition from doctors and firefighters; pilot for the series.
Deadly Maneuvers. Mercenaries capture B.A., Face and Murdock, and hold them at a dairy farm, leaving Tawnia and Hannibal to devise a rescue.
Semi-Friendly Persuasion. The team abides by a cult's nonviolent philosophy to defeat corrupt townspeople who burned their community building.
Curtain Call. The team recalls incidents of Murdock's bravery and loyalty while he lies badly wounded by a bullet meant for Hannibal.
Bullets and Bikinis. The team flies to Miami to wage war against gangsters threatening to take over a resort hotel owned by two sisters.
The Bend in the River. Tawnia recruits the team to save her adventurer fiancé, captured by Amazon River pirates while searching for a lost city.
The Bend in the River. The captured team discovers a secret in the jungle and must enlist El Cajon's assistance to destroy a deadly installation.
Fire!. The team helps a fire chief (Stepfanie Kramer) save her one-truck company from takeover by a larger operation.
Timber!. The team helps brother-and-sister lumberjacks thwart a crooked union boss intent on driving them out of business.
Double Heat. The team interrupts a war between crime syndicates to rescue a government witness's (Dana Elcar) daughter (Leah Ayres).
Veteran. Banner must go to the police to save a former Vietnam hero from a sniper.
Dark Side. Self-experimentation releases Banner's primitive impulses; guest Rosemary Forsyth.
Free Fall. A corrupt politician sabotages an aerial exhibition team employing Banner; guest Sam Groom.
The First. Banner investigates legends of another scientist, dead 30 years, who underwent a Hulk-type metamorphosis.
Sanctuary. To save a wounded immigrant boy, Banner poses as a visiting priest; guests Henry Darrow, Diana Muldaur.
Patterns. A factory owner in debt to the mob labels Banner as his partner.
Love at First Sight. Newlywed Caitlin (Sheena Easton) fears Sonny's undercover assignment at a dating service will make her a widow.
A Rock and a Hard Place. Two music executives attempt to cash in on Caitlin's resurrected career by exposing Sonny's drug-dealer alter-ego.
Knight of the Rising Sun. Ninja warriors kidnap an industrialist's (Ken Swofford) adopted son, thinking him a descendant of their leader.
Voodoo Knight. A voodoo princess and her henchmen will stop at nothing to possess an ancient crown being held at a private vault company.
Knight of the Phoenix. A dying millionaire (Richard Basehart) rescues a badly wounded undercover police officer and gives him a new identity.
Knight of the Phoenix. Michael Knight, fully healed, seeks revenge on the electronics-industry saboteurs who killed his partner.
Deadly Maneuvers. Michael helps an Army officer (Devon Ericson) investigate her colonel father's strange death.
Good Day at White Rock. A timid sheriff arrests Michael for interfering with a gang of angry motorcyclists; guest Anne Lockhart.
Slammin' Sammy's Stunt Show Spectacular. KITT is scheduled to participate in an auto-stunt show whose organizers fall prey to a greedy developer.
Just My Bill. Michael and KITT guard a controversial senator opposing water-power legislation.
Not a Drop to Drink. A cattle rancher (Jason Evers) asks Michael to foil politicians who want to steal his water rights.
No Big Thing. Jailed for a traffic infraction, Devon sees a cellmate murdered.
Death Probe. Steve joins forces with Soviet experts to stop a Venus probe which is loose and wreaking havoc in Wyoming.
Danny's Inferno. Kidnappers stalk a boy (Lanny Horn) who has accidentally invented a new form of thermochemical energy; guest Frank Marth.
The Fires of Hell. A sheriff and a congressman sabotage an oil-drilling site; guests Ken Swofford, Bruce Glover.
The Infiltrators. Steve goes undercover as an amateur boxer to infiltrate a suspected assassination team made up of alien expatriates.
Carnival of Spies. Steve has doubts about an East German scientist who left a conference complaining of heart problems.
U-509. Steve must choose between his life and the lives of thousands when a blackmailer threatens to use nerve gas.
Max. The bionic dog is kidnapped by foreign agents while Jaime lies helpless in a hospital bed.
The Over-the-Hill Spy. To catch an elderly Soviet spy, OSI must reactivate an agent (Richard Erdman) made bitter by forced retirement.
All for One. Jaime meets a computer whiz (Franklyn Ajaye) while undercover in college to learn who has been stealing from OSI.
The Pyramid. Jaime is trapped beneath a Southern California pyramid with an alien (Eduard Franz) predicting the destruction of Earth.
The Antidote. Max and Chris Williams seek the antidote to a poison given to Jaime and a Soviet diplomat.
The Martians Are Coming, the Martians Are Coming. While working on a project to track unidentified flying objects, Dr. Wells is abducted in a flying saucer.
Sanctuary Earth. First on the scene of a crashed satellite, Jaime meets an alien princess who claims enemy agents are after her.
Deadly Music. Jaime scuba dives as part of an OSI assignment, but is unaware she carries a device to attract sharks.
Trust Doesn't Rust. Two thieves unleash KITT's prototype KARR, programmed without an instruction to protect human life.
Inside Out. Michael poses as a mob's getaway driver to stop a robbery and rescue a woman blackmailed into helping.
The Wedworth Townsend Act. An assembly bill to create a paramedic program meets opposition from doctors and firefighters; pilot for the series.
Mascot. Gage promises to care for an injured woman's dog; the paramedics save five lives including a diabetic and a man trapped on a ledge.
Botulism. An injured cameraman proves to have more than a broken leg, leading Brackett to search for a botulism source; guest Susan Seaforth.
Cook's Tour. DeSoto and Gage deliver a baby over the father's protests; DeSoto worries about a dinner he is planning for the station-house crew.
Brushfire. A canyon fire threatens the residents of a housing development and keeps the paramedics on round-the-clock duty; guest Tony Dow.
Dealer's Wild. DeSoto and Gage talk down an airplane flown by a teenage boy whose father, the pilot, suffered a heart attack while at the controls.
Nurses Wild. The paramedics hold a demonstration for student nurses, one of whom interests Gage; the hospital staff saves a robber and his victim.
Publicity Hound. Gage resents media attention given to a paramedic (Gary Crosby) from another squad; Brackett clashes with a tycoon over a diagnosis.
Weird Wednesday. The paramedics and hospital staff deal with a stubborn elderly woman (Jeanette Nolan), a parachutist in a tree and other odd cases.
Dilemma. Gage and DeSoto rescue an elderly couple from an elevator crash; Brackett berates a forgetful student nurse; a girl irritates Gage.
Trouble on Wheels. B.A., Hannibal and cohorts infiltrate a car factory to capture a gang of ruthless auto-parts thieves.
The Island. Drug smugglers operating from a tropical island hold the team's former Vietnam medic (James Callahan) captive.
Showdown!. A gang of toughs jeopardizes the team's reputation by posing as the four and terrorizing rodeo performers and spectators.
Sheriffs of Rivertown. A U.S. oil company wants order restored in a makeshift community housing workers for a South American electrical-power plant.
The Bells of St. Mary's. An all-girl band from Face's old orphanage hires the team to go after a corrupt record-company executive (Robert Desiderio).
Hot Styles. The team infiltrates the fashion world to rescue Face's girlfriend (Markie Post) from her kidnapper (Richard Lynch).
Breakout!. Hannibal devises an elaborate escape plan after B.A. and Murdock are mistaken for accomplices in a robbery and sentenced to work on a chain gang.
Cup A'Joe. B.A. and Murdock help a diner owner and his daughter fight a corrupt tycoon who wants their land for an off-ramp.
The Big Squeeze. The team works from a pub to stop a loan shark (Joseph Sirola) from terrorizing small businesses; guest Wings Hauser.
A Minor Problem. Banner seeks an antidote for bacteria contaminating a deserted town; guest Nancy Grahn.
Half Nelson. A wrestler's exaggerated boasts get Banner in trouble with the mob.
